source: MAFF/GIZ, "Guidelines for Banana Export from Cambodia to China" (2022), section 4
text:
Packing houses that handle fresh fruit for export to China must be separately authorized by GACC, in addition to the orchard registration described elsewhere. Packing houses seeking this authorization are expected to demonstrate:

- Traceability systems linking every batch of packed fruit back to a specific registered orchard, with clear batch/lot numbering carried through from field to carton.
- Documented hygiene and food-safety practices covering the facility itself (clean water source, pest-proofing, waste management) and worker practices (handwashing, protective clothing where relevant).
- A functioning quality inspection step before packing, so that fruit with visible pest damage, disease symptoms, or defects is sorted out before it reaches export cartons.
- Proper recordkeeping of inspection results and any corrective actions taken, since inspectors from both the Cambodian side and, periodically, the Chinese side may review these records or physically inspect the facility.
- A clear, documented management structure with someone accountable for compliance, since authorization can be suspended or revoked if serious or repeated non-compliance is found.

The guide frames packing-house authorization and orchard registration as two separate approvals that both have to be in place and kept current — an exporter needs a registered orchard supplying an authorized packing house, not just one or the other.
